items.line: Vanity Fair posts an excerpt from Matthew Cole's book. Cole writes that a source told him in 2020 that the Dutch government had hacked Jared Kushner's phone and watched him use a Dubai bank account holding hundreds of millions of dollars. These are claims in the excerpt. Not checked here.

Alexis Ohanian says he named Reddit 21 years ago, that people called it a horrible name, and that he overruled them as CEO. He says the company's own account is now making the "I read it on reddit" joke. Not checked here.

James Talarico, the Democratic nominee for US Senate in Texas, says there is something deeply wrong with a political system that allows one trillionaire to buy his own personal US Senator. His post quotes another post. Not checked here.

Streamer QTCinderella says people were late to her wedding and that it set the wedding back. She asks viewers to stop hating on someone on behalf of another streamer and says drama clippers have farmed it. The post does not name who she means.
Enes Kanter Freedom says he was kicked out of a WNBA game for the second time in a row, and says it was for supporting women. Not checked here.
The Associated Press reports that Virginia state Sen. L. Louise Lucas is charged with drug trafficking and money laundering, citing the Justice Department. Not checked here.
Reporter Dan Lamothe says in an exclusive that Pete Hegseth wanted Gen. Dwight Eisenhower's globe for his office and that Hegseth's staff broke it. He says he has photos. Not checked here.

Investor m. stanfield says an unnamed executive at a large property management company told him over dinner that the US apartment market is the worst that person has seen in 40 years. These are secondhand claims. Not checked here.

PopBase, an entertainment news account, says Getty Images has filed for bankruptcy amid mounting debt and competition from AI-generated images, and plans to restructure and become privately owned. Not checked here.
The account unusual_whales says the stock with the ticker $MRNA is down 24% today to $187 and describes options-market price levels it calls support and resistance. Not checked here.
The Hollywood Reporter reports that actor Tom Skerritt, a star of "Picket Fences" and "Alien", has died at 93. Not checked here.

Madison Mills, a reporter, posts an Axios scoop saying major US banks are detecting unauthorized third-party AI agents inside customer accounts. Axios says it is told this by unnamed bank and industry executives. Not checked here.
Sky News posts a breaking alert saying Barclays is cutting 5,000 jobs in an efficiency drive led by AI. The post links to Sky’s own report. Not checked here.

NFL reporter Dov Kleiman says the Bengals are under heavy criticism online for not greeting Vice President JD Vance, and that many Republicans are calling for the NFL to fine them. He says most of the team did not shake Vance's hand. Not checked here.
BBC Breaking reports that US President Donald Trump has been ordered to sit for a deposition by 11 December in his defamation case against the BBC. The post links to the BBC report. Not checked here.

Andrew Curran says Quest Diagnostics has been hacked and patient data exposed, and that the company serves roughly half of US hospitals and physicians. He says an investigation is ongoing. Not checked here.
Massimo, an account that shares science and history clips, says the IBM 7094 became the first computer to sing a song in 1961, "Daisy Bell". The post carries a 38-second video. Not checked here.

The account America posts a video clip. It says Texas Democratic Senate nominee James Talarico says he hates Voter ID and calls it anti-American, and it says 84% of Americans support Voter ID. The clip and both claims were not checked here.
SportsCenter posts a video with the caption "That's a travel." and asks how many steps LaMelo took. The video was not checked here.

Anthony Slater posts a video and says Yaxel Lendeborg told reporters he "lost all respect" for Luka Doncic after facing him, because Doncic was "complaining the entire game." Slater quotes Lendeborg adding "I told him he sucks." Not checked here.
DiscussingFilm says Jack Lowden, Callum Turner and Josh O'Connor are among the actors in the mix to be the next James Bond and are doing final auditions. It credits Deadline. Not checked here.

Fabrizio Romano quotes Harry Kane on the Ballon d’Or. Kane says he would like to know the result now, that his family is nervous, and that he understands France Football wants to keep it quiet so all the stars can attend.
La-Ndlovu posts a joke: there should be an app where people upload their bills and bored billionaires swipe right to pay them.

The Athletic reports, citing unnamed sources, that Knicks assistant coaches did not get championship rings on banner night and that many longtime Garden employees will not get rings. It also says a September "free ring" email to staff was a phishing test. Story linked.

The NBA account posts that LeBron James had 17 points, 10 rebounds, 5 assists and 3 steals in his home debut in Philadelphia and says his team came back from 29 points down, the largest comeback of his 24-year career.

The account eastdakota gives attack figures for a PHP bug called #php2shell. It says Cloudflare saw thousands of exploit attempts before the announcement, tens of thousands in the first 45 minutes after, and now millions. These are the poster’s counts. Not checked here.

Dexerto says the AI K-pop group BABYQUEEN is facing backlash after its creators "impregnated" one of its members. It says they did it to write her out of the group and manage fewer AI personalities. Not checked here.
The poster kalaelizabeth says a BioWare developer leaked a Mass Effect 5 trailer on Reddit, called "MASS EFFECT UNIVERSE". The post carries a 2-minute video. The leak is not checked here.
